title: Foundation for Public Code cannot be joined, but its Standard is a recognised credential
content:
The Foundation for Public Code is a route that cannot be taken by joining it. Membership is restricted to wholly publicly owned organisations, so a private vendor cannot become a member; the relationship available is compliance with what the Foundation publishes rather than affiliation with the Foundation itself.

What it publishes is the Standard for Public Code, and its work is codebase stewardship — quality auditing, community nurturing, and helping public bodies and vendors reuse public code. It stewards Open Zaak among others, was founded in 2019, and is based in Amsterdam.

The commercially relevant part is that meeting the Standard for Public Code is a credential Dutch public buyers recognise. That converts an unreachable organisation into a published bar to clear: the work is making a codebase pass the Standard, and the payoff is a signal buyers already know how to read without any relationship having to be established first.
